source_name: IBV NBS FinNext — AML & Compliance conference
why_relevant: Dedicated SK AML/compliance conference with a published agenda; session titles map directly onto the AML package/AMLA readiness topics that SK banks and PSPs are actually working on, plus speaker affiliations reveal who leads those programmes.

source_name: Verlag Dashöfer SK — seminars/webinars (eseminare.sk, dashofer.sk, vdu.sk)
why_relevant: Commercial training publisher active in SK since 1997; schedules seminars on AML, financial fraud and financial-sector legislation. Seminar scheduling is demand-driven, so the calendar is a market-timing proxy for which obligations firms are scrambling to meet.

source_name: Kurzy.sk / Skolenia.sk — SK training-course aggregators
why_relevant: Aggregate the catalogues of many SK training providers in one searchable index — the cheapest way to detect a new regulation-themed course appearing anywhere in the market, then snowball to the provider.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia finančníkov (asocfin.sk) — conferences and events
why_relevant: Corporate treasury/finance association; its conference topics reveal how payments and reporting regulation is landing on the corporate/treasury side (instant payments, VoP, e-invoicing), which is a demand signal ahead of bank product changes.

source_name: Zlatá minca — SK financial product awards (nominations & results)
why_relevant: 20-year-old SK awards programme with a ~200-member expert jury across bank, insurance and investment categories, plus 'Most Innovative Bank' and 'Discovery of the Year'. Nomination lists are effectively a curated inventory of live products and new market entrants (e.g. Revolut, Interactive Brokers appearing) — an indirect map of who is regulated-and-active in SK.

source_name: PwC Slovakia — DORA / regulatory advisory pages and dictionary
why_relevant: Big-4 SK practice pages and webinars are commercially motivated to appear exactly when a compliance deadline becomes billable, so publication timing is a demand indicator; content also states the SK-specific scope and deadlines advisors are selling against.

source_name: Highgate.sk — SK law-firm commentary on PSD3/PSR
why_relevant: SK legal/advisory boutiques publish Slovak-language explainers when clients start asking; a cluster of firm posts on one regulation is a weak signal that SK PSPs are entering implementation. Also names the SK-specific licensing consequences (authorisation, transition of existing providers).

source_name: FinReport.sk — SK financial-market trade media (fintech/regulation desk)
why_relevant: Covers SK conference sessions, association positions and regulatory debates in detail (e.g. the first public discussion of a national fintech strategy at Finweek). Useful as a recap channel when an agenda or speech is not itself published.

source_name: Konferencie.sk — SK conference directory
why_relevant: Cross-industry SK event directory; a cheap discovery layer for finance/banking/payments events run by organisers not otherwise on the radar, which then get promoted to tracked sources.

source_name: NBS – Štatistický zberový portál (ŠZP / Statistics Collection Portal)
why_relevant: The operational submission channel (live since 1.1.2016, replacing STATUS-DFT) through which banks, payment institutions and EMIs file statistical and supervisory returns. Its public documentation carries report catalogues, technical specs, validation rules and operational notices with dates.

source_name: NBS – Metodické informácie pre vykazujúce subjekty (Methodological information)
why_relevant: Holds the methodological manuals reconciling ECB/ESCB statistical reporting with EBA supervisory reporting (FINREP/COREP) for Slovak reporting agents — the authoritative mapping between taxonomies and national return codes.

source_name: NBS – Číselníky a registre (Code lists and registers)
why_relevant: National code lists / registers underpinning the reporting taxonomy (sector codes, instrument codes, entity registers). Machine-readable reference data needed to interpret any SK return and to resolve reporting-entity identities.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 7/2023 o predkladaní výkazov platobnými inštitúciami, inštitúciami elektronických peňazí, PSP v obmedzenom rozsahu a bankami
why_relevant: The binding legal instrument setting the payments-sector reporting taxonomy and hard deadlines (semi-annual Ps(NBS)04-02..08-02 by last calendar day of 3rd month after period; quarterly Ps(NBS)09-04 by last day of following month; monthly Pb(NBS)12-12). Directly answers 'which PSP files what, when'.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 8/2021 o predkladaní výkazov bankami, pobočkami zahraničných bánk a obchodníkmi s CP na štatistické účely (konsolidované znenie)
why_relevant: Core banking statistical reporting measure: enumerates report codes (Cp(NBS)01-12, Mk(NBS)00-12/02-12/03-12/04-12 etc.), periodicity and the 10th-working-day monthly deadline pattern. Consolidated-text PDF is the cleanest machine-parsable calendar for bank statistical returns.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 9/2022 o predkladaní výkazov bankami a obchodníkmi s CP na účely zberu údajov podľa osobitných predpisov
why_relevant: Supervisory-side (not purely statistical) reporting measure for banks — the national hook under which EBA ITS-based FINREP/COREP style data collection is operationalised in SK.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS z 24. marca 2025 o predkladaní výkazov poskytovateľmi služieb kryptoaktív (MiCA reporting)
why_relevant: Newest reporting-obligation layer adjacent to payments (CASPs under MiCA). Signals how NBS extends its return taxonomy to new licence types — a leading indicator of future PSP/EMI reporting changes.

source_name: NBS – Metodika na vypracúvanie hlásenia SLUZ(NBS)1-04 (payment/services reporting methodology PDF)
why_relevant: Concrete per-return methodology document showing the level of detail NBS publishes (codes for payment services, country of origin/destination classification). Template for what to harvest for every return code.

source_name: NBS – Podmienka I: zásady a definície pre zber štatistických údajov o výkonnosti, transakciách a podvodoch (PI/AISP licensing condition)
why_relevant: Ties licensing to the statistical/fraud data-collection obligation for payment institutions and AISPs — shows the obligation exists from day one of authorisation and defines the data scope (performance, transactions, fraud).

source_name: NBS – Všeobecné usmernenia pre účastníkov prevádzky IS STATUS-DFT / legacy transition notices
why_relevant: Operational guidance for the legacy STATUS-DFT collection channel and connection instructions for entities not yet migrated. Useful for historical continuity of return codes and for understanding channel migrations that shift deadlines.

source_name: NBS – Harmonogram zverejňovania údajov (data release calendar)
why_relevant: Forward-looking dated schedule of NBS statistical data releases — the publication-side counterpart to submission deadlines, and the most machine-readable dated artefact NBS publishes for statistics.

source_name: NBS – Predstihový kalendár zverejňovania údajových kategórií SDDS Plus (advance release calendar, PDF)
why_relevant: IMF SDDS Plus advance release calendar under NBS gescia — half-year-ahead dated commitments per data category. Hard, verifiable dates with long lead time; ideal for a deadline-tracking dataset.

source_name: NBS – Hlásenia pre devízovú ohlasovaciu povinnosť (FX reporting obligation)
why_relevant: A distinct, often-overlooked reporting stream (balance-of-payments/FX) that binds banks and some non-banks, with its own forms and deadlines separate from the prudential and payments streams.

source_name: EBA – Reporting frameworks (DPM, XBRL taxonomies, validation rules)
why_relevant: Upstream authority for FINREP/COREP taxonomies that Slovak banks must apply. Framework releases (e.g. v4.2 applying from Q4 2025, xBRL-CSV from reference date 31 March 2026) set the dated change agenda NBS then implements nationally.

source_name: ECB Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 (ECB/2020/59) amending payments statistics Regulation 1409/2013 (ECB/2013/43)
why_relevant: The EU legal basis for PSP payment-statistics reporting (quarterly and semi-annual tables, fraud data) that NBS transposes into its Ps(NBS)/Pb(NBS) returns. Defines the taxonomy and the outer deadline envelope; national deadlines are set by NBS and may be tighter.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR – Program štátnych štatistických zisťovaní / spravodajská povinnosť (reporting units)
why_relevant: The non-NBS statistical reporting leg: the Programme of State Statistical Surveys (a generally binding legal regulation under Act 540/2001 Z. z.) imposes reporting duties on legal entities including financial firms, with mandatory electronic filing since 1.1.2016.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR – zber.statistics.sk (electronic data collection portal + quality reports/metadata)
why_relevant: ŠÚ SR's electronic collection interface and its published metadata/quality reports — the ŠÚ SR counterpart to NBS's ŠZP, and the machine-readable metadata layer describing each survey (periodicity, deadlines, methodology).

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) – payment card issuing/acquiring statistics
why_relevant: Industry-association aggregation of member-bank card statistics on a regular cadence — an indirect read on what data banks compile and when, and a cross-check on NBS payment statistics.

source_name: EPI.sk / ASPI (Wolters Kluwer SR) – consolidated texts of NBS opatrenia
why_relevant: Commercial legal databases carrying consolidated, amendment-tracked texts of NBS reporting measures — often clearer than the gazette PDFs for determining the currently effective deadline table.

source_name: SlovakFintech – legislatíva overview for payment/fintech reporting obligations
why_relevant: Community-maintained pointer list mapping SK payment/fintech legislation including NBS reporting opatrenia — useful for snowballing to instruments not surfaced by NBS site search.
